title: Tailwind CSS Small Examples
description: Use these small Tailwind CSS examples with the tools described in each lesson. Read the expected result before you try a change.

examples.title: Meet utility classes
examples.description: A utility class has one small style job.
examples.output: With Tailwind output.css loaded, the words appear bold and dark blue.

examples.title: Add inner and outer space
examples.description: Padding is space inside a box. Margin is space outside a box.
examples.output: The box has inner padding, a border and extra space below its outside edge.

examples.title: Choose readable text
examples.description: Text size and line spacing work together.
examples.code:
Garden club

We plant seeds and watch them grow.
examples.output: The heading is large and bold. The paragraph has a normal text size with roomy lines.

examples.title: Use colour and borders
examples.description: A background fills a box, while a border marks its edge.
examples.code:
<aside class="bg-yellow-100 text-yellow-950 border border-yellow-400 rounded-lg p-4">
  Bring water for the plants.
</aside>
examples.output: The note has a pale yellow background, dark words, a yellow border and rounded corners.

examples.title: Line up a row with flex
examples.description: Flex layout places child boxes in a row by default.
examples.output: The label and count sit in a row, aligned through the middle, with space between them.

examples.title: Make grid columns
examples.description: A grid can arrange boxes in rows and columns.
examples.output: Four items form two rows with two columns each.

examples.title: Start small then grow
examples.description: A responsive prefix applies a class from a chosen screen width upwards.
examples.code:
First book
Second book
examples.output: The books stack at small widths. At the default md breakpoint and above, they form two columns.

examples.title: Show keyboard focus
examples.description: A state prefix changes a style when an element is in that state.
examples.code:
<button class="rounded bg-blue-800 px-4 py-2 text-white hover:bg-blue-900 focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-4 focus-visible:outline-blue-800">
  Read a story
</button>
examples.output: The button darkens on hover and shows a visible outline during keyboard focus.

examples.title: Use the dark variant
examples.description: The dark variant supplies styles for a dark colour setting.
examples.code:
<article class="bg-white text-slate-900 dark:bg-slate-900 dark:text-white p-4">
  Evening reading
</article>
examples.output: The card uses light colours normally and dark colours when the system prefers a dark theme.

examples.title: Name a theme colour
examples.description: A theme variable adds a design choice that Tailwind can turn into utilities.
examples.output: After rebuilding, classes such as bg-leaf use the new green colour.

examples.title: Keep class names complete
examples.description: Tailwind finds class names by reading your source files as text.
examples.output: Both complete class strings can be discovered during a Tailwind build. The selected value is the success string.

examples.title: Put a card together
examples.description: A small card combines several single-job classes.
examples.code:
Book of the week

A story about a moon garden.

See the book list
examples.output: The card has a limited width, round border, inner space and an underlined link. The /books address must exist in your own site.
